trial_court: Family Court, Hamirpur, H.P. (HMA Petition no.51/2018 RBT 37 of 2020)
case_name: Sarita Kapil vs Rajesh Kumar Kapil
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The parties were married in 2006 and have a son. The husband filed for restitution of conjugal rights under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The trial court allowed the application. The wife appealed.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party alleging cruelty to prove specific instances of physical and verbal abuse.
legal_principles.held: Though the appellant contended that she had stayed away from the respondent on account of physical and mental abuse meted out to her by the respondent, no specific instances of any physical violence and verbal abuse by the respondent had been put to her in her cross-examination.

legal_principles.principle: A party's attitude towards their child can be an indicator of their commitment to the family.
legal_principles.held: Her attitude was indifferent not only towards the respondent but also to her child.

outcome.final_order: The appeal is preferred by the appellant challenging the judgment allowing the respondent's application for restitution of conjugal rights. The application for condonation of delay is allowed, and the appeal is disposed of.

keywords: Protection of Women from DV Act
